history.summary: Paramekkavu Bhagavathy Temple on the east side of Swaraj Round in Thrissur is regarded as one of the largest Bhagavathy temples in Kerala. Legend says a Nair family head's devotion drew the Goddess to accompany him home on his umbrella; after Vadakkunnathan's consecration the Devi's chaitanya was transferred under a Paro (Ilanji) tree, giving the shrine its name Parokkavu (later Paramekkavu). Sakthan Thampuran ordained the Thrissur Pooram into two rival groups - Paramekkavu side and Thiruvambadi side - each with its own elephants, panchavadyam and kudamattam display. The eight-armed wooden idol (consecrated 1997) is visible only during the Karkidakam Chandatta ritual; otherwise devotees worship the golden Sree Kovil covering. The temple devaswom runs Paramekkavu Vidya Mandir school.

name: Paramekkavu Bhagavathy Temple
town_description: Thrissur is a major city in central Kerala, often called the cultural capital of the state for its temples, pooram festivals and classical arts. Paramekkavu temple stands on Round East, about 500 m from Thiruvambadi temple and just off the Vadakkunnathan precinct at the city's core. It is easily reached from Thrissur railway station.

travel.road: On Round East, Thrissur city; well served by KSRTC and city buses; parking in temple complex
